title: Severe hypertension with headache and blurred vision, 50-year-old woman
provenance: Vignette written 2026-09-30 for the evaluation harness; expected answers extracted from the cited documents.

intake.complaint: Severe headache and blurred vision since this morning.
intake.history: Hypertension; stopped her medicines two months ago.

triage.note: Both extractors: level 2. A: Level 2 comes from three cells. Adult Vital Signs Level 2 column (p7, x~131): 'BP > 220/130 with symptoms' (228/132 with headache and blurred vision) and 'Severe Pain (8 - 10)' (pain 8). HEADACHE complaint Level 2 column (p9, x~131): 'Pain Score > 7'. Primary triage Critical First Look Level 2 column (p4, x~246): 'Severe Pain'. The headache row's 'Visual / Speech difficulty' is Level 3 (x~244). No Level 1 cell applies (GCS 15, airway and circulation intact). If there is an altered mental state or neuro deficit (headache L2 cells), the level stays at 2. B: Level 2 comes from several cells: the vital-signs cells 'BP > 220/130 with symptoms' (x~131, p7) and 'Severe Pain (8 - 10)' (x~131, p7), the HEADACHE complaint cell 'Pain Score > 7' (x~131, p9), and the Primary Triage cell 'Severe Pain' (x~246, p4). 'Sudden Vision Loss' is a Level 3 cell (EYE/VISION, x~244, p9). No Level 1 cell applies.

disposition.note: The CPG says patients with hypertensive emergency should be admitted for immediate intervention and monitoring, without naming the unit. HDU/ICU is preferred because titrated IV infusions and close BP monitoring are needed (nitroprusside needs intra-arterial monitoring). Ward admission is acceptable. If assessment finds no acute target-organ damage (urgency), the urgency pathway applies: rest, oral agents, and admit or refer if she does not respond. / A hypertensive emergency needs admission and IV titration with close monitoring, so HDU/ICU is preferred. A ward is acceptable if there is no acute target-organ damage (urgency pathway: oral agents, and the CPG says 'may be admitted'). Discharge is not acceptable: BP is above 220/130 with symptoms and pain score 8.

adjudication.method: two independent extraction passes (A, B); agreed items scored

A: Emergency vs urgency: blurred vision plus headache suggests acute target-organ involvement (encephalopathy or retinopathy). However, the HTN CPG 2018 counts grade III/IV retinopathy without overt target-organ symptoms as urgency. Primary label is emergency; urgency is accepted as an alternative.
The HTN CPG table contradicts itself on the BP floor: 160/90 on p53 vs 160/100 on p17/p59. The gold uses 160/100.
Disposition unit is not specified by the source (only 'admitted'). HDU preferred is my choice.
Analgesia for pain score 8 headache is not covered by a specific KKM statement for this presentation, so it is omitted.
CT brain is optional: the ICH CPG requires neuroimaging for stroke-like symptoms, and the intake reports no focal deficit.
B: Emergency or urgency cannot be settled from the intake alone. Headache is listed as a 'non-specific' symptom (p49), and the CPG classes grade III/IV retinopathy without overt target-organ symptoms as urgency (p51). Blurred vision plus pain 8 makes emergency (possible encephalopathy) the more defensible label, so urgency is kept as an acceptable alternative.
For urgency the CPG says there is 'no role for intravenous BP lowering drugs' (p51). IV agents are therefore not listed as forbidden, because this case is most likely an emergency.
CT brain is marked required on the strength of the ICH CPG (to confirm or exclude ICH), not the HTN CPG, which does not list imaging for severe hypertension.
